quotes.text: Agents don't share your business goals. They share the literal instructions you feed them. That disconnect is the principal agent problem in a tech wrapper.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames AI agent risk in one crisp economic analogy.

quotes.text: That oversight often means requiring human approval before an agent makes potentially risky changes like sending data externally or modifying records across core systems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete guidance on where human approval belongs in agent workflows.

quotes.text: The point is not to chase perfect transparency, because generative reasoning will always be partly opaque. The point is to give yourself enough surface data to monitor patterns, catch anomalies, and enforce accountability before problems drift beyond your reach.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets a realistic goal for agent observability instead of perfect explainability.

quotes.text: Agents aren't replacing managers. They're forcing you to sharpen management itself. The research is clear this is just the principal agent problem wearing a hoodie. They hold the data, you hold the liability, and the only real fix is guided autonomy plus constant oversight.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of the manager's new accountability for digital coworkers.

chapters.title: Managers as bosses of digital workers
The three pieces every agent needs: memory, entitlements, tools

takeaways: AI agents combine memory, entitlements and tools, and each of these is both a superpower and a failure point if left unmanaged.
Agents follow literal instructions rather than business intent, creating a principal-agent problem and information asymmetry that leaves managers accountable for opaque decisions.
Inventory and tier your agents by risk, set escalation thresholds with human-in-the-loop approvals, and red-team critical agents with RBAC, MFA, DLP and audit logs in place.
hook: AI agents are arriving in Teams, SharePoint and Dynamics with real entitlements and tool access, but without understanding your boundaries. This episode is for managers and IT leaders who need to govern these digital coworkers. You get a simple framework, practical controls and first steps to keep agents useful, safe and aligned.
